==English==
{{wp|<dab>}}
{{wp|Week-day names}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰegʷʰ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|Saterday}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sæterdæġ}}, earlier {{m|ang|sæternesdæġ|t=Saterday|lit=Saturn's day}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*Sāturnas dag}}; a translation of {{der|en|la|diēs Saturnī}}, equivalent to {{af|en|Saturn|day}}. Compare {{cog|sco|Seturday}}, {{cog|fy|saterdei|t=Saturday}}, {{cog|nl|zaterdag|t=Saturday}}, {{cog|nds-de|Saterdag|t=Saturday}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q131}}The seventh day of the [[week]] in many religious traditions, and the sixth day of the week in systems using the ISO 8601 norm; the [[Jewish]] [[Sabbath]]; it follows [[Friday]] and precedes [[Sunday]].
#: {{syn|en|Seventh Day|q=Quakerism}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Laura He|title=China may have to bail out one of its poorest provinces|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2023/04/27/economy/china-guizhou-province-debt-crisis-bailout-intl-hnk|date=2023-04-27|passage=The Beijing-based firm — one of four funds created by the Chinese government in 1999 to process the bad loans of state-owned banks — announced '''Saturday''' that it would send a group of 50 experts to the province to help it “prevent and defuse risks” and “bail out” the real estate industry.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528053956/https://edition.cnn.com/2023/04/27/economy/china-guizhou-province-debt-crisis-bailout-intl-hnk}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Kevin Liptak|title=With stiff tariffs he promised now in place, Trump opens a new trade war|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/02/01/politics/tariffs-trump-campaign-promise|date=2025-02-01|passage='''Saturday'''’s tariffs are unlikely to be Trump’s last. The president said himself said in the Oval Office that additional tariffs could come by mid-February on chips, pharmaceuticals, steel, aluminum, copper, oil and gas imports – along with tariffs on the European Union – all threats that few would discount given his willingness to follow through on the North American and China tariffs on '''Saturday'''.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250805160458/https://www.cnn.com/2025/02/01/politics/tariffs-trump-campaign-promise}}
